data.name: Aabir
data.gender_notes: Aabir is used as a male name in Arabic and Urdu naming tradition.
data.short_meaning: Passer-by; one who crosses or traverses; traveller
data.long_meaning: Aabir (عابر) is an Arabic name meaning “Passer-by; one who crosses or traverses; traveller”. It is the active participle of ʿabara 'to cross, to pass over', from the root ʿ-b-r. The root also yields ʿibrah ('lesson, example') and ʿabīr ('fragrance'), so the same letters carry several distinct classical senses. The name shares this root with Aabeer (fragrance), which is a different word in the same family.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aabir carries the meaning Passer-by; one who crosses. Any spiritual reading placed on the name is interpretive and is labelled as such; the lexical meaning is the documented core.
data.etymology: From Arabic ʿābir (عابر) 'passer-by, one who crosses', active participle of ʿabara, from the root ʿ-b-r.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aabir total 18, reducing to 9. Number 9 is associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What does the name Aabir mean?
faq.a: Aabir means Passer-by; one who crosses or traverses; traveller.

faq.q: What is the origin of the name Aabir?
What language does the name Aabir come from?
faq.a: Aabir is used in Arabic and Urdu.

faq.q: Is Aabir a boy's name or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aabir is used as a male name.

faq.q: How is Aabir written in Arabic?
faq.a: Aabir is written عابر in Arabic, Urdu and Pashto, and आबिर in Devanagari.

faq.q: What is the linguistic root of Aabir?
faq.a: The root of Aabir is ʿ-b-r (ع-ب-ر), from ʿābir (عابر).

faq.q: What is the etymology of Aabir?
faq.a: From Arabic ʿābir (عابر) passer-by, one who crosses, the active participle of ʿabara, from the root ʿ-b-r.

faq.q: Does Aabir appear in the Qur'an?
faq.a: No. Aabir is not itself a Qur'anic name; it is used in Muslim naming tradition.

faq.q: Is Aabir the same as Aabeer?
faq.a: No. Aabir (عابر) means passer-by. Aabeer (عبير) means fragrance. They share the root ʿ-b-r but are different words.

faq.q: What other words come from the root ʿ-b-r?
faq.a: The root ʿ-b-r also yields ʿibrah (lesson, example) and ʿabīr (fragrance), alongside ʿābir (passer-by).

faq.q: Is the meaning of Aabir verified?
faq.a: Yes. The meaning Passer-by rests on the Arabic active participle ʿābir, from the root ʿ-b-r.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Aabir?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aabir total 18, reducing to 9. Number 9 is traditionally associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Aabir?
faq.a: Variants and alternative transliterations include Abir and Aaber.

faq.q: Where is the name Aabir used today?
faq.a: Aabir circulates chiefly in Arabic and Urdu naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
